title: Updating Wills, Powers of Attorney, and Contact Forms
html:
A memo from Fr. Bede, our Prior, dated October 7:

Over the coming weeks, the community will be updating three important documents for each monk — part of ordinary stewardship, to keep records current and reduce confusion when something serious happens. Instructions and a schedule will follow once Abbot Brendan returns from retreat; nothing is needed from anyone immediately.

A Last Will and Testament gives legally binding instructions for what must be settled after death, so a monk's personal circumstances and the monastery's interests are both addressed clearly under civil law.

A Power of Attorney lets someone act on a monk's behalf in legal, financial, and medical matters if he's ever unable to decide for himself. The revised version also builds in guidance from Catholic moral teaching — on the dignity of human life, proportionate treatment, ordinary care, nutrition and hydration, and pain management.

A Who to Contact form isn't a legal document — it just lists who the monastery should reach out to, with current contact information, in case of serious illness, hospitalization, emergency, or death.

Joanna will serve as Medical Witness where needed, and Br. Thomas as Notary Public.

title: The Story Behind Abbot Brendan's November 21 Blessing
html:
We've already shared that Abbot Brendan's Abbatial Blessing is set for Saturday, November 21 — here's a bit more on how that date came to be.

Ordinarily, a newly elected Abbot receives the Abbatial Blessing within three months of election. But since Abbot Brendan is still working through diaconate ordination first, the Congregation's Abbot President, Abbot Jonathan R. Licari, OSB, consulted the Presidents Council and formally dispensed with that three-month rule so the Blessing could follow his diaconate ordination instead.

Abbot Licari's letter closed with every good wish "as you work toward diaconate ordination and Abbatial Blessing" — worth keeping both in prayer as that day approaches.

title: A Note from Fr. Dominic, Our New Prior
html:
Fr. Dominic sent this letter to the community as he settles into his new role as Prior:

Dear Confreres,

Thank you for your prayers as I take on my new role of service as Prior. Due to other duties in the school, Fr. Bede has graciously agreed to take responsibility for most of the scheduling (I will still handle pastoral coordination, but he will print the schedules). Ordinarily, I will have the morning office hours and Fr. Bede will have the afternoon office hours. Please plan to bring any extraordinary requests or permissions in the morning rather than the afternoon. I will not be present at Sext during the days of school.

A few reminders for all of us:

  1. Travel Forms for overnight trips other than pastoral assignments are signed by the Abbot. Copies must be given to the Prior, the Subprior, the Abbey Business Office, the MC, and the Choirmaster (if you are a chanter).
  2. We owe it to each other to prepare for our duties as Matins Acolyte, Table Reader, and Celebrant. If we cannot be present, we should arrange for or inform a substitute so they can prepare.
  3. The Table Reader should be ready to begin reading after the table blessing. Ordinarily, this duty will require the monk to leave Vespers at the beginning of the Angelus.
  4. Table readers continue reading until the bell — please don't pause for lengthy periods near 6:30.
  5. If you are absent from Matins/Lauds or Vespers, please let me know beforehand if possible.
  6. Cars are ordinarily parked under the carport, not at the back door, except for loading and unloading — and please turn off all accessories when you park.

Pax,
Fr. Dominic, Prior

title: Road Widening Near the Abbey — Public Comments Due August 21
html:
The Alabama Department of Transportation is moving ahead with a project to widen AL-69 and replace the bridge over Eight Mile Creek near the Abbey, and the community is being asked to submit public comments before an August 21 deadline.

Fr. Paschal and Fr. Bede attended a public meeting on the broader Hwy-278 expansion on August 5 at East Elementary School, alongside area parents and faculty. A few notes from that meeting: right-of-way acquisition is expected to begin in 2027, with construction starting in 2029; the roughly $34 million project runs on federal grants and a congressional earmark, and likely can't grow beyond that; and because of funding limits, the expansion — a five-lane road with curb and gutter — will only run from Fourth Street to about Richard Avenue before tapering back into the existing road, which raises its own concern about simply shifting the traffic bottleneck. Alabama's highway director is retiring, and a meeting with State Senator Garland was discussed as a way to help secure further funding.

Closer to home, the Abbey is asking anyone willing to submit a comment specifically on the AL-69 widening, since it affects the Abbey's own entrance — there's real concern about traffic congestion and about the safety of students, pilgrims, and retreat and festival guests coming in and out, and a push for a traffic light there. Comments can be emailed to AL69-Widening@dot.state.al.us and are due by August 21, 2026.

Worth keeping in prayer — for a safe, sensible resolution at our own front gate.

title: Faculty Return for In-Service Days
html:
Faculty and staff return August 5–7 for this year's In-Service days. This year's formation theme is "Encountering Suffering in Our Own Lives and the Lives of Those We Serve," opened by Fr. Joel and carried further by Sr. Jane Dominic, O.P. — a good one to hold in prayer, both for the faculty sitting with it and for whatever it is meant to address.

The days include Mass in the Abbey Church, and on Thursday the faculty join the monks for Midday Prayer (Sext) and lunch in the monastic refectory. Fr. Paschal and Fr. Joel are giving the year's President's and Headmaster's reports, and Rachael and Fr. Dominic are leading a session on the school's vision. The rest of the week is routine training and classroom preparation.
